Maaco of Independence, Missouri Scammed me $1000 (Details Inside, Cautionary Tale)

Posting this as a cautionary tale of anyone considering taking their car to a Maaco for labor. I cannot describe how horrendous this whole ordeal has been, and I do not expect to ever get my money back.

Maaco of Independence, MO scammed me of $1000. I paid this shop $1000 as a down payment for labor and paint on my car 6 weeks ago on September 3rd. When I paid the shop, the manager, Travis, told me that the car would be ready in approximately 2 weeks. I knew this was likely an early estimation, so at first when the car was delayed I was not upset. However, every time I called the shop and spoke to Lori (receptionist) after the first delay, they would just extend the promise to "it will be finished xDay", and so on, and any time that I asked for the actual status of the car, no one knew, or no one was at the shop/available.

Finally, after 5 weeks on (10/08) I was getting nervous having not seen my car in a month (the shop is an hour away from me). I called the manager, Travis, directly and he apologized and said that it was their fault for having poor communication. He promised to make it up for me, and told me the car would definitely be in the paint booth that Thursday. I told him I would need to pick the car up the following weekend, regardless of it's status, as my girlfriend and I could not go on with sharing a single car. She has two jobs and attends university, and I have a full time position. He acknowledged this and promised the car would be ready. Additionally, he promised to send me a photo of the car so I would have an idea of what they're working with. I never received this photo, and later I found out why.

I called Travis that Friday to confirm that the car was ready, and he immediately took a different tone and simply said "I don't think your car is ready buddy", and brushed off the issue. I told him I would be at the shop tomorrow regardless.

When I arrived, I found that the shop staff had been COMPLETELY replaced. When I walked in the door and asked for Travis, everyone seemed to take defense and told me that Travis got suspended for poor dealing with customers. The phone was ringing constantly while I was there. I asked to go back and see my car, and none of them even knew which car was mine, and were confused when I described it to them.

Finally, one of them took me to the back of the shop, and through the heaps of cars I saw mine. It had not even been touched. The car had just been parked there, for 6 weeks, with no changes whatsoever. On later inspection, I also found that I had cables missing from my radio.

I spoke with the new manager (Chris) and he agreed that I would need a refund. He promised to talk to Ryan, the owner of the shop, and that I should come by on 10/17 to meet with him. When I arrived, everyone was leaving the shop and they said Ryan may not be there as he got tied up in a meeting. I had called Maaco and spoke to Chris repeatedly that day and TOLD THEM to make sure that Ryan was there, and the exact time I would be there. They all simply evacuated as soon as I showed up. Chris gave the the phone number of another "corporate" person to call, who gave me the same runaround that Ryan was in town to issue refunds, and told me that he would call Ryan and tell him to call me. I told him to make sure Ryan called me that night, and I never heard from him.

This is unacceptable and I'm already in the process of filing a claim with the Business Bureau, and will also contact the local news channel. Apparently, I am far from the only customer of that shop to have complaints, so there should be at least a few of us. Your shop has blatantly stolen money from me, has robbed me of time, and has treated me absolutely pathetically since I first trusted your shop with my car and down payment.

These are photos of what my car looked like after sitting at Maaco for 6 weeks after I had already put $1000 down. It was the EXACT same as it was before I took the car in. All of the new body components had been installed by me prior to the car being brought in.

Better Business Bureau is a private business. Think of it like Yelp for old-school brick-and-mortar shops. And just like Yelp, you can negotiate with them for a better score or to get old complaints "Disappeared". Good call with the news channel, though. With any luck, they'll get even more stories called in after they broadcast.

Have you talked to an attorney yet? Cases like this are what Small Claims Court is precisely for, and if you signed a service agreement, it sounds like an open-and-shut case.

Unless you paid cash, file a dispute with your bank or credit card company. They'll need some basic info from you, and then they'll fight on your behalf to recover the funds from the merchant. This type of dispute will be 1 of 2 reasons - If they did absolutely nothing, it will be disputed as "Non-Receipt of Merchandise or Services." If they did some work, but obviously didn't complete the job, it will be disputed as "Merchandise / Services not as described."

This is something all US card issuers are required to offer their customers, and since they will be dealing with the merchant, you don't have to play the corporate run-around game anymore.

EDIT: I would recommend this before filing a claim in small claims court. It requires much less effort on your end, there is a good chance you will recover the funds without ever seeing court, and if they fight this to the end, you have that much more proof you tried to resolve the matter before going to court AND you will have whatever documents in hand that the merchant tried to use to prove their case.

Take them to small claims and do it fast. A lot of those national chains are just franchised shops like a subway or a mcdonalds. If that's the case then you can't get paid back from the chain if the franchise goes under. It sounds like they might be if shit is going that badly. "Ryan" might be the absentee owner or negligent manager. You'll want to get your case heard before they declare bankruptcy. Hopefully they'll just give you your money back when you file the papers

Sue them for the amount you gave them plus like $40 per day for the loss of the use of your vehicle while they had it. Change the "loss of use" amount to what it would've cost you to get a rental, document the actual cost of the rental. Don't cling to that money, but you might be entitled to it so ask. If you aren't entitled to it the court wont give it to you, but you wont get it if you don't ask. It might help encourage the shop to return your money too.

Take screenshots of your phone history showing every date and to.e and length of call when you contacted them. Make copies of any documentation they have provided you. Write down everything you remember about what you were told and when you were told it.

You wont know what you'll need so make sure you've got it all. Be happy if you get your money back. The best way to do that is to make the store realize that it will be too much trouble to fight you on it. If they're going broke then they'll end up screwing some other poor sap instead.
